beijing.localVibe: Beijing is confident, fast, and a bit bossy — in a good way. Locals gather at dawn in parks for tai chi, opera singing, and kite flying. At night, the hutongs turn into bars and grill spots.
funFacts: Beijing was the capital of six major dynasties and has the world's largest palace complex, the Forbidden City.
The city has over 3,000 years of history but its metro system is one of the world's busiest and most modern.
Beijing roast duck was originally called 'shao ya' (burned duck) and was a favorite of emperors and diplomats.

dialect.meaning: A respectful 'you' with the Beijing erhua.
No way / nothing can be done — a classic Beijing shrug.

famousPeople.name: Mao Zedong
famousPeople.desc: The founding father of the People's Republic of China declared the new China from Tiananmen Gate in Beijing.

famousPeople.name: Cao Xueqin
famousPeople.desc: The author of Dream of the Red Chamber, China's greatest novel, lived in Beijing and wrote about its aristocratic families.

famousPeople.name: Mei Lanfang
famousPeople.desc: The legendary Peking opera artist changed how the world saw Chinese theater.

shanghai.localVibe: Shanghai is China's most cosmopolitan city — fast, fashionable, and slightly competitive. Locals love a good bargain, late-night supper, and discussing real estate over coffee.
funFacts: The name Shanghai means 'Upon the Sea' and it grew from a small fishing village into one of the world's largest cities in just 150 years.
Shanghai has the world's longest metro network by route length, and it keeps growing.
The famous xiaolongbao soup dumplings were perfected in Shanghai's Nanxiang town.

dialect.meaning: Hello in Shanghainese — sounds warmer than standard Mandarin.
Extremely / very — used to emphasize how good something is.

famousPeople.name: Lu Xun
famousPeople.desc: China's greatest modern writer lived in Shanghai during the 1920s and 1930s and wrote sharp social critiques.

famousPeople.name: Zhou Enlai
famousPeople.desc: The first premier of China studied and worked in Shanghai before becoming a statesman.

famousPeople.name: Yao Ming
famousPeople.desc: The retired NBA superstar and one of China's most recognizable athletes was born in Shanghai.

guangzhou.localVibe: Guangzhou is loud, humid, and obsessed with food. Locals will drive across town for the best dim sum, and tea houses fill up early on weekends. The city is practical, business-minded, and famously welcoming to outsiders.
funFacts: Guangzhou is one of the world's oldest continuously active trading ports, with over 2,200 years of history.
The Canton Fair, held twice a year in Guangzhou, is China's largest trade fair and has been running since 1957.
Cantonese cuisine is so central to local identity that locals joke, 'We eat everything with four legs except tables.'

dialect.phrase: 食咗饭未 (sik6 zo2 faan6 mei6)
dialect.meaning: Have you eaten? — the classic Cantonese greeting.
Please / thank you for a service — used constantly.

famousPeople.name: Sun Yat-sen
famousPeople.desc: The founding father of modern China launched multiple revolutions from Guangzhou and is still honored across the city.

famousPeople.name: Kang Youwei
famousPeople.desc: A major reformer of the late Qing dynasty came from Guangdong and advocated for modernizing China.

famousPeople.name: Zeng Chengwei
famousPeople.desc: A contemporary Guangzhou-born composer whose music has been performed internationally.

shenzhen.localVibe: Shenzhen is China's youngest major city — fast, tech-focused, and full of people from somewhere else. Nobody is from Shenzhen, so everybody is from Shenzhen. The pace is 24/7, but weekend hikes and beach trips keep people sane.
funFacts: Shenzhen was a small fishing village of about 30,000 people in 1980; today it is a megacity of over 17 million.
It is home to Huawei, Tencent, DJI, and BYD — four of the world's most influential tech companies.
Shenzhen has the most border crossings to Hong Kong and is one of the world's busiest ports by container volume.

dialect.meaning: Handsome guy — also used to call a young male waiter casually.
Check / bill, borrowed from Cantonese and used widely.
Get it done / sort it out — a very Shenzhen attitude.

famousPeople.name: Ren Zhengfei
famousPeople.desc: Founder of Huawei, born in Guizhou, built one of the world's largest telecom companies from Shenzhen.

famousPeople.name: Ma Huateng (Pony Ma)
famousPeople.desc: Founder of Tencent and the creator of WeChat, born in Shantou and based in Shenzhen.

famousPeople.name: Wang Chuanfu
famousPeople.desc: Founder of BYD, the electric vehicle and battery giant, started his empire in Shenzhen.

chengdu.localVibe: Chengdu is the capital of chill. Locals say the best job is one that pays enough for mahjong, hot pot, and tea. Parks fill with ear-cleaning barbers, card players, and pandas who barely move faster than the locals.
funFacts: Chengdu is home to the Chengdu Research Base of Giant Panda Breeding, the world's best-known panda sanctuary.
It has been the capital of six local kingdoms and is famous for never being conquered by outside forces for long.
Sichuan province, with Chengdu at its heart, has over 70,000 rivers and is nicknamed 'the land of abundance.'

dialect.meaning: Comfortable / great / just right — the Chengdu life motto.
Go for it / cheer up — used at football matches and bars.

dialect.phrase: 摆龙门阵 (bǎi lóng mén zhèn)
dialect.meaning: To chat or gossip — the city's favorite pastime.

famousPeople.name: Du Fu
famousPeople.desc: One of China's greatest poets built his Thatched Cottage in Chengdu during the Tang dynasty and wrote many of his most famous works there.

famousPeople.name: Li Bai
famousPeople.desc: The legendary Tang poet spent important years in Sichuan and is said to have drunk his way through Chengdu's taverns.

famousPeople.name: Zhang Yimou
famousPeople.desc: The internationally acclaimed film director was born in Xi'an but launched his career in Chengdu.

xian.localVibe: Xi'an carries 3,000 years of history but is also a city of students, street food, and late-night noodle shops. Locals are proud, direct, and have a dry sense of humor. The ancient city wall is now a jogging track, and the Muslim Quarter never sleeps.
funFacts: Xi'an was the eastern starting point of the Silk Road and served as the capital of 13 Chinese dynasties.
The Terracotta Army, discovered by farmers in 1974, contains over 8,000 soldiers, horses, and chariots — no two faces are alike.
Xi'an is one of the few Chinese cities where you can still walk on a complete Ming-dynasty city wall.

dialect.phrase: 克里马擦 (kè lǐ mǎ cā)

dialect.meaning: To chat or shoot the breeze — a favorite local activity.

famousPeople.name: Qin Shi Huang
famousPeople.desc: The first emperor of unified China, buried near Xi'an with his Terracotta Army.

famousPeople.name: Yang Guifei
famousPeople.desc: One of the Four Beauties of ancient China, closely linked to the Tang dynasty court in Xi'an.

famousPeople.name: Zhang Yimou
famousPeople.desc: The acclaimed film director was born in Xi'an and often draws on northwestern Chinese culture in his work.

hangzhou.localVibe: Hangzhou is elegant, green, and slightly smug about its lake. Locals bike around West Lake, drink Longjing tea, and complain about the summer humidity. The city balances tech wealth with classical Chinese aesthetics.
funFacts: West Lake is a UNESCO World Heritage site and has inspired Chinese poets and painters for over 1,000 years.
Hangzhou is home to Alibaba, one of the world's largest e-commerce companies, founded by Jack Ma in an apartment here.
The Grand Canal, which runs through Hangzhou, is the longest artificial river in the world and over 1,700 years old.

dialect.meaning: Kid / child — a Hangzhou way to refer to young people.
Comfortable in the stomach — the perfect description of a satisfying meal.
Pretty good / not bad — typical Hangzhou understatement.

famousPeople.name: Su Shi (Su Dongpo)
famousPeople.desc: The Song dynasty poet and governor built the famous Su Causeway across West Lake.

famousPeople.name: Jack Ma
famousPeople.desc: Founder of Alibaba Group, one of China's most influential entrepreneurs, started his company in Hangzhou.

famousPeople.name: Yue Fei
famousPeople.desc: The legendary Song dynasty general is buried and honored near West Lake.

guilin.localVibe: Guilin is where China switches to cruise mode. Life moves at the pace of the Li River, locals start the day with a bowl of rice noodles, and retirees practice tai chi under karst peaks that look like a watercolor painting. The city is laid-back, proud of its scenery, and quietly confident that it has the best landscape in the country.
funFacts: The name Guilin (桂林) literally means 'Forest of Sweet Osmanthus' — the city is named after the fragrant trees that once blanketed the streets.
The 20-yuan Chinese banknote features the Li River scenery near Xingping, just downstream from Guilin.
The karst mountains around Guilin are over 300 million years old and inspired countless traditional Chinese landscape paintings.
Yangshuo, a town near Guilin, became famous after the movie The Painted Veil (2006) was filmed there.

dialect.meaning: Eat rice noodles — the local greeting-equivalent for breakfast.
Fun — Guilin people use it the way others say 'cool' or 'nice.'
Slow down / take it easy — perfectly matches the riverside pace.

famousPeople.name: Li Zongren
famousPeople.desc: A Guilin-born general and vice president of the Republic of China, whose former residence is now a museum in the city.

famousPeople.name: Liu Sanjie
famousPeople.desc: Legendary Zhuang folk singer from the Guangxi region; her story is celebrated in the nightly Impression Liu Sanjie show on the Li River near Yangshuo.

famousPeople.name: Bai Juyi
famousPeople.desc: The Tang-dynasty poet who served as an official in Guilin and wrote some of his earliest poems about the region's landscape.

wuhan.localVibe: Wuhan is three cities pretending to be one: Wuchang, Hankou, and Hanyang. Locals are hot-tempered, funny, and loyal to their breakfast streets. Summer heat is brutal, but the river breeze and a bowl of hot dry noodles make it bearable.
funFacts: Wuhan is called 'the Thoroughfare of Nine Provinces' because it sits at the crossroads of China's rail and river networks.
The 1911 Wuchang Uprising in Wuhan started the Xinhai Revolution that ended China's last imperial dynasty.
Locals take breakfast so seriously that '过早' (guo zao) means 'passing the morning' through a parade of street food.

dialect.meaning: Eat breakfast — a serious Wuhan ritual.
What are you doing? — direct and friendly.

famousPeople.name: Li Hongzhang
famousPeople.desc: A powerful late Qing statesman whose Hanyang Arsenal helped modernize China's military industry.

famousPeople.name: Qian Xuesen
famousPeople.desc: A world-famous aerospace engineer and rocket scientist who studied in Wuhan.

famousPeople.name: Liu Yifei
famousPeople.desc: The actress known as 'Fairy Sister' in China spent part of her childhood in Wuhan.

suzhou.localVibe: Suzhou is refined, garden-proud, and quietly wealthy. Locals speak softly, drink Biluochun tea, and believe life is better beside a canal. The city is the classic southern Chinese ideal of culture, silk, and slow beauty.
funFacts: Suzhou's classical gardens are UNESCO World Heritage sites and date back over 1,000 years.
The city is known as the 'Venice of the East' because of its extensive canal network, especially in the Pingjiang Road area.
Suzhou silk has been the luxury fabric of choice for Chinese emperors and was traded along the Silk Road.

dialect.meaning: Hello in Suzhou dialect — soft and elegant.
Do you want to buy? — often heard in old markets.

famousPeople.name: Fan Zhongyan
famousPeople.desc: Northern Song dynasty statesman and poet, best known for his line 'Be the first to worry about the world's troubles and the last to enjoy its pleasures.'

famousPeople.name: Tang Yin
famousPeople.desc: One of the Four Masters of the Ming dynasty, a painter and poet from Suzhou.

famousPeople.name: I. M. Pei
famousPeople.desc: The world-famous architect was born in Suzhou and designed the city's Suzhou Museum.

nanjing.localVibe: Nanjing is dignified, bookish, and slightly melancholic. As the capital of six dynasties, it carries history heavily but also knows how to enjoy duck, salted duck, and evening walks along the Qinhuai River. Locals are proud and opinionated.
funFacts: Nanjing means 'Southern Capital' and has served as the capital of six Chinese dynasties plus the Republic of China.
The city wall of Nanjing is the longest, largest, and best-preserved city wall in the world, built by the Ming dynasty.
Nanjing ducks are so beloved that locals say 'No duck can leave Nanjing alive.'

dialect.phrase: 多大四啊 (duō dà sì a)
dialect.meaning: What's the matter? — a Nanjing way of asking what's up.
Generous / bold — a compliment to someone's character.
Excellent / top-notch — often used for duck dishes.

famousPeople.name: Sun Yat-sen
famousPeople.desc: The father of modern China is buried in Nanjing at the Sun Yat-sen Mausoleum on Purple Mountain.

famousPeople.name: Zhu Yuanzhang
famousPeople.desc: The Hongwu Emperor, founder of the Ming dynasty, built Nanjing's great city wall and made it his capital.

famousPeople.name: Liu Xie
famousPeople.desc: A literary critic from the Southern Dynasties who wrote The Literary Mind and the Carving of Dragons.

harbin.localVibe: Harbin is China's Russian-flavored ice city. Locals are hearty, direct, and fond of beer, sausage, and arguing about winter. The city turns into a frozen wonderland every January, and ice cream is sold on sticks even at -20°C.
funFacts: Harbin hosts the world's largest ice and snow festival, with sculptures the size of buildings lit up in neon colors.
Russian influence is visible in the onion-domed Saint Sophia Cathedral and the city's love for red sausage and kvass.
Harbin Beer, founded in 1900, is one of China's oldest and most popular beer brands.

dialect.meaning: What are you doing? — Northeastern directness.
Definitely / of course — a Northeastern catchphrase.

famousPeople.name: Qiao Yu
famousPeople.desc: A celebrated lyricist from Northeast China whose songs are known across the country.

famousPeople.name: Wang Liping
famousPeople.desc: A composer from Heilongjiang known for music in classic Chinese TV dramas.

famousPeople.name: Harbin Symphony Orchestra
famousPeople.desc: One of China's oldest orchestras, founded in 1908, reflecting the city's Russian musical heritage.

hefei.localVibe: Hefei is the quiet overachiever of eastern China. Once known as a sleepy provincial capital, it is now a booming tech and science hub. Locals are practical, proud of their universities, and surprisingly loyal to stinky mandarin fish and duck fat biscuits.
funFacts: Hefei is the birthplace of the quantum communication satellite Micius and hosts the University of Science and Technology of China, one of the country's top science schools.
The city has transformed from a manufacturing base into a center for AI, electric cars, and quantum computing.
Lord Bao, the famous honest official of the Song dynasty, held office in Hefei and is buried in the city's Bao Park.

dialect.phrase: 搞七廿三 (gǎo qī niàn sān)
dialect.meaning: Making a mess / causing trouble — classic Hefei slang.
Good to talk / easy to discuss.

famousPeople.name: Bao Zheng (Lord Bao)
famousPeople.desc: The legendary incorruptible judge of the Song dynasty served in Hefei and is one of China's most beloved historical figures.

famousPeople.name: Li Hongzhang
famousPeople.desc: The powerful late Qing diplomat and statesman was born in Hefei's rural area.

famousPeople.name: Yang Zhenning
famousPeople.desc: Nobel Prize-winning physicist studied and taught at the University of Science and Technology of China in Hefei.

kunming.localVibe: Kunming is the 'City of Eternal Spring' and feels like it. Locals eat mushrooms, barbecue, and rice noodles at all hours, and the weather is so mild that many homes don't have air conditioning. The city is relaxed, multicultural, and a gateway to Yunnan's wild landscapes.
funFacts: Kunming has an average annual temperature of about 15°C, giving it the nickname 'Spring City.'
The Stone Forest, a UNESCO site nearby, is a maze of limestone pillars formed over 270 million years.
Yunnan is one of the most biodiverse provinces in China, home to over 18,000 plant species and many ethnic minority groups.

dialect.meaning: Great / excellent — the classic Kunming compliment.
What are you buying? — used like 'What's up?' in some contexts.
Where are you going? — local Kunming Mandarin.

famousPeople.name: Zheng He
famousPeople.desc: The Ming dynasty explorer and admiral was born in Kunming's region and led seven great maritime expeditions.

famousPeople.name: Nie Er
famousPeople.desc: The composer of China's national anthem, March of the Volunteers, was born in Kunming.

famousPeople.name: Joseph Rock
famousPeople.desc: An Austrian-American explorer and botanist who lived in Yunnan for decades and introduced its culture to the West.

dalian.localVibe: Dalian is China's most European-feeling coastal city. Wide boulevards, tram lines, and seafood markets give it a relaxed seaside energy. Locals are proud of their clean air, football history, and the fact that their city is nothing like typical northern China.
funFacts: Dalian was once a Russian port, then a Japanese colony, and you can still see European and Japanese architecture mixed into the cityscape.
It is famous for China's first tram line, which still runs through the city center.
The city is known as the 'Fashion City' of China and hosts an annual international fashion festival.

dialect.meaning: Extremely enjoyable / satisfying — a Dalian favorite.
Don't drag it out — Northeastern bluntness.
Eat food — a local way to say 'let's eat.'

famousPeople.name: Sun Jihai
famousPeople.desc: One of China's most famous footballers, born in Dalian, which is known for its strong football culture.

famousPeople.name: Chi Zhiqiang
famousPeople.desc: A Dalian-born actor well known in Chinese television and film.

famousPeople.name: Dalian Shide Football Club
famousPeople.desc: Once one of China's most successful football clubs, representing the city's deep football culture.

tianjin.localVibe: Tianjin is Beijing's cheeky neighbor — cheaper, funnier, and better at comedy. Locals are famous for their quick wit, love of seafood, and a dialect that sounds like a stand-up routine. The city blends colonial-era architecture with a working-class port soul.
funFacts: Tianjin was once home to nine foreign concessions, leaving behind a colorful mix of Italian, French, British, and German architecture.
The city is famous for its traditional comic dialogue art, xiangsheng, with masters like Ma Sanli and Guo Degang coming from here.
Tianjin is the birthplace of the Chinese industrial revolution and once hosted China's first modern railway, telephone, and post office.

dialect.meaning: What is this? — Tianjin's playful version of Mandarin.

dialect.phrase: 倍儿哏儿 (bèi r gén r)
dialect.meaning: Really funny — the highest Tianjin compliment.
What are you doing? — sounds almost musical in Tianjin dialect.

famousPeople.name: Ma Sanli
famousPeople.desc: One of China's greatest xiangsheng (comic dialogue) masters, beloved for his Tianjin wit.

famousPeople.name: Guo Degang
famousPeople.desc: The modern king of Chinese crosstalk and founder of Deyun She, born in Tianjin.

famousPeople.name: Zhang Xueliang
famousPeople.desc: The 'Young Marshal' who held Tianjin as a key stronghold during the Republican era.

jinan.localVibe: Jinan is the city of springs, where locals drink tea made with water straight from the ground. It is understated, educated, and proud of being the home of Shandong culture. Life moves slower than in Qingdao, and people are direct and warm.
funFacts: Jinan has over 70 natural springs and is known as the 'City of Springs' — the most famous is Baotu Spring.
The city is a historic center of Confucian culture and is close to Qufu, Confucius's hometown.
Jinan's sweet pancakes and crispy fried dough sticks are considered a classic northern breakfast.

dialect.meaning: A respectful term for a man, similar to 'sir' or 'mate.'
Very good / excellent — classic Jinan praise.
What — used at the end of questions in Jinan dialect.

famousPeople.name: Li Qingzhao
famousPeople.desc: One of China's greatest female poets of the Song dynasty was born in Jinan, and her memorial hall is a city landmark.

famousPeople.name: Xin Qiji
famousPeople.desc: A famous Song dynasty poet and military leader also from Jinan, known for his bold ci poetry.

famousPeople.name: Confucius
famousPeople.desc: Though born in nearby Qufu, Jinan served as a key Confucian cultural center for centuries.

nanchang.localVibe: Nanchang is a proud revolutionary city with a surprisingly spicy food scene. Locals love chili peppers, street-side barbecue, and evening strolls along the Gan River. It feels like a city that has seen history but is now young and hungry.
funFacts: Nanchang is where the People's Liberation Army was founded on August 1, 1927, a date still celebrated as China's Army Day.
Tengwang Pavilion, rebuilt many times, is one of China's most famous ancient towers and inspired Tang dynasty poetry.
Nanchang people are so fond of spice that even breakfast noodles come with a chili kick.

dialect.meaning: Eat food — a Jiangxi way to say 'let's eat.'
What — Nanchang dialect for asking about something.

famousPeople.name: Wang Bo
famousPeople.desc: The Tang dynasty poet who wrote the famous Preface to the Pavilion of Prince Teng about Nanchang's landmark.

famousPeople.name: Zhu De
famousPeople.desc: One of the founding marshals of the People's Liberation Army had strong ties to Nanchang's revolutionary history.

famousPeople.name: Mei Yaochen
famousPeople.desc: A Song dynasty poet from the region known for his plain, realistic style.

chongqing.localVibe: Chongqing is a mountain city built on fog, spice, and ambition. Locals are straight-talking, tea-obsessed, and proud of their hot pot. The city looks like a cyberpunk movie set, with monorails passing through apartment blocks and riverside lights that never dim.
funFacts: Chongqing is the world's largest city by area and one of China's four direct-controlled municipalities.
It was China's wartime capital during the resistance against Japan and served as the government's home for years.
Chongqing hot pot is famous for its numbing Sichuan peppercorns, and locals say you haven't really visited until you've eaten it in a riverside alley.

dialect.meaning: Great / comfortable — used in Chongqing just like in Chengdu.
Go for it — a battle cry and a toast.
Okay / sure — the classic Southwestern reply.

famousPeople.name: Deng Xiaoping
famousPeople.desc: The architect of China's reform era was from nearby Guang'an and spent formative years in the Chongqing region.

famousPeople.name: Zhou Enlai
famousPeople.desc: The beloved premier spent important revolutionary years in Chongqing during the wartime capital period.

famousPeople.name: Jiang Zemin
famousPeople.desc: The former president of China studied electrical engineering at Chongqing's National Central University.

qingdao.localVibe: Qingdao is China's breezy, beer-soaked beach city with a German aftertaste. Locals are laid-back, seafood-obsessed, and fiercely proud of their Tsingtao beer. Red-tiled roofs and blue sea give it a Mediterranean feel rare in China.
funFacts: Qingdao was a German concession from 1898 to 1914, and the European architecture remains in the old town.
Tsingtao Beer, founded by Germans in 1903, is one of China's most exported beer brands and hosts an annual international beer festival.
The city hosted the sailing events for the 2008 Beijing Olympics.

dialect.meaning: Drink beer — the Qingdao weekend ritual.
Eat clams — almost always paired with beer.
Silly or crazy — a playful Qingdao insult.

famousPeople.name: Kang Youwei
famousPeople.desc: The late Qing reformer spent his final years in Qingdao and is buried there.

famousPeople.name: Wang Lijun
famousPeople.desc: A former police chief known for his role in a major political scandal, though his legacy is controversial.

famousPeople.name: Tsingtao Brewery
famousPeople.desc: Founded by Germans in 1903, it became a symbol of Qingdao and one of China's most famous brands.

xiamen.localVibe: Xiamen is China's island city of coffee, sea breeze, and slow afternoons. Locals are polite, tea-loving, and proud of their Gulangyu Island, a car-free music-themed island just offshore. The city feels more Southeast Asian than northern Chinese.
funFacts: Xiamen is famous for Gulangyu Island, a UNESCO World Heritage site with colonial-era villas and no cars.
The city faces Taiwan across the strait and is one of the main gateways between the two sides.
Xiamen University is often ranked as one of China's most beautiful campuses.

dialect.meaning: Wow / surprise — a very Xiamen-style exclamation.
What? — a mild, casual Hokkien-influenced expression.
You're welcome — polite and common in Xiamen.

famousPeople.name: Tan Kah Kee
famousPeople.desc: A Xiamen-born businessman and philanthropist who funded schools and universities across China and Southeast Asia.

famousPeople.name: Koxinga (Zheng Chenggong)
famousPeople.desc: The Ming loyalist who expelled the Dutch from Taiwan set out from the Xiamen region.

famousPeople.name: Shu Ting
famousPeople.desc: A famous contemporary poet from Xiamen and a leading figure in the Misty Poets movement.

fuzhou.localVibe: Fuzhou is a tea-and-sea city where life moves at a polite, deliberate pace. Locals are proud of their Min River culture, Buddhist temples, and seafood soups. It's less flashy than Xiamen but deeply rooted in Fujian's trading history.
funFacts: Fuzhou is the capital of Fujian and one of the historic starting points of Chinese maritime trade and emigration.
The city is famous for Three Lanes and Seven Alleys, a historic district that hosted scholars, officials, and writers for centuries.
Fuzhou fish balls are prized because they are stuffed with pork, not just fish paste.

dialect.meaning: Hello in Fuzhou dialect — the Min language sounds very different from Mandarin.
Really / true — a common Fuzhou expression.
Very tired — a casual Min-dialect phrase.

famousPeople.name: Lin Zexu
famousPeople.desc: The Qing dynasty official who destroyed British opium at Humen was born in Fuzhou's Houguan county.

famousPeople.name: Bing Xin
famousPeople.desc: A beloved modern Chinese writer and poet from Fuzhou, known for her gentle children's literature.

famousPeople.name: Yan Fu
famousPeople.desc: A famous translator and intellectual from Fuzhou who introduced Western social science to China.

zhengzhou.localVibe: Zhengzhou is the crossroads of China — a railway hub where north, south, east, and west meet. Locals are practical, noodle-loving, and proud of being at the heart of Chinese civilization. The city is busy, no-nonsense, and full of Henan hospitality.
funFacts: Zhengzhou is near the ruins of Yin, the capital of China's Shang dynasty, one of the earliest known Chinese dynasties.
The city is one of China's largest railway hubs, connecting almost every major city by high-speed rail.
Henan cuisine, especially its braised noodles and mutton soup, is hearty and famous across northern China.

dialect.meaning: Okay / good / yes — the most famous Henan word, used in almost every conversation.
What are you doing? — Henan style.

famousPeople.name: Du Fu
famousPeople.desc: One of China's greatest Tang poets was born in Henan, near Zhengzhou's cultural region.

famousPeople.name: Li Shangyin
famousPeople.desc: A Tang dynasty poet from Henan famous for his romantic and allusive verse.

famousPeople.name: Deng Xiaoping
famousPeople.desc: China's reform leader traced part of his revolutionary career through the Henan region.

sanya.localVibe: Sanya is China's tropical playground, where winter tourists escape the cold and locals live in flip-flops. The city is relaxed, beach-focused, and proud of its coconut trees, seafood, and year-round summer vibe.
funFacts: Sanya is the southernmost city on Hainan Island and is known as 'China's Hawaii.'
Buddhist culture is strong here — the Nanshan Temple hosts a 108-meter tall Guanyin statue by the sea.
The city attracts millions of Russian tourists every winter, earning it a nickname as Russia's favorite Chinese beach town.

dialect.meaning: Hello / how are you? — a Hainan-style greeting.
Eat rice — locals use it the way others say 'let's eat.'
What are you doing? — influenced by Hainan Min language.

famousPeople.name: Huang Daopo
famousPeople.desc: A legendary Yuan dynasty textile pioneer said to have learned advanced weaving techniques in Hainan.

famousPeople.name: Su Dongpo
famousPeople.desc: The Song dynasty poet was exiled to Hainan and wrote about its remote tropical beauty.

famousPeople.name: Hou Xun
famousPeople.desc: A modern Hainan-born entrepreneur who helped promote the island's tourism industry.

haikou.localVibe: Haikou is Hainan's relaxed capital, full of coconut trees, old骑楼 (arcade houses), and seafood markets. Locals start the day with老爸茶 (dad tea) and move slowly in the tropical heat. It feels like a permanent vacation city with real local life.
funFacts: Haikou's Old Town is famous for its qilou arcade buildings, a mix of Chinese and Southeast Asian colonial styles.
The city is the gateway to Hainan Island, China's largest tropical island and a growing free-trade zone.
Haikou is one of China's most livable cities, with clean air, parks, and a slower pace than mainland megacities.

dialect.meaning: Drink tea — locals say 'eat tea' like many southern Chinese.
Nothing much — a relaxed Hainan reply.

famousPeople.name: Hai Rui
famousPeople.desc: A famous Ming dynasty honest official served in Hainan and is commemorated in Haikou.

famousPeople.name: Qiu Jin
famousPeople.desc: The revolutionary feminist had connections to Hainan's early modern intellectual circles.

famousPeople.name: Huang Daopo
famousPeople.desc: The legendary Yuan dynasty weaver is linked to Hainan's cultural heritage.

lhasa.localVibe: Lhasa is the spiritual roof of the world. Prayer flags, butter lamps, and the smell of juniper incense fill the air. Locals are deeply religious, hospitable, and move at a pace shaped by altitude and devotion. Every step here feels like a pilgrimage.
funFacts: Lhasa means 'Place of the Gods' in Tibetan and sits at 3,650 meters above sea level.
The Potala Palace was the winter residence of the Dalai Lamas and is now a UNESCO World Heritage site.
Jokhang Temple is considered the most sacred temple in Tibet and draws pilgrims from across the plateau.

dialect.meaning: Good luck / auspiciousness — the classic Tibetan greeting.
How are you? — a polite Tibetan phrase.

famousPeople.name: Songtsen Gampo
famousPeople.desc: The 7th-century Tibetan emperor who unified Tibet and established Buddhism as a state religion.

famousPeople.name: Dalai Lama
famousPeople.desc: The spiritual leaders of Tibet, whose historical residence was the Potala Palace in Lhasa.

famousPeople.name: Milarepa
famousPeople.desc: A revered 11th-century Tibetan yogi and poet, one of Tibet's most beloved spiritual figures.

lijiang.localVibe: Lijiang is an ancient Naxi town of cobblestones, canals, and red lanterns. Locals are proud of their Dongba culture, love singing and dancing in the square, and keep the old town alive with live music and yak butter tea. It feels like stepping into a storybook.
funFacts: Lijiang Old Town is a UNESCO World Heritage site and one of the best-preserved ancient towns in China.
The Naxi people have a unique pictographic writing system called Dongba script, one of the last living pictographic scripts in the world.
Jade Dragon Snow Mountain looms over Lijiang and is considered sacred by the Naxi people.

dialect.meaning: Naxi people often greet with a smile and 'Nashi' — a warm, simple hello.
Cheers — as in most of China, but Lijiang toasts often include local rice wine.
Walk slowly — a gentle Lijiang farewell, matching the town's pace.

famousPeople.name: Joseph Rock
famousPeople.desc: An Austrian-American explorer and botanist lived in Lijiang for decades and introduced Naxi culture to the world.

famousPeople.name: Xuan Ke
famousPeople.desc: A Naxi musician who helped preserve and popularize traditional Naxi ancient music.

famousPeople.name: He Wuming
famousPeople.desc: A modern Lijiang-born writer who wrote about Naxi traditions and the old town.

dali.localVibe: Dali is a laid-back lakeside town where backpackers, artists, and Bai locals mix. The old town sits between Erhai Lake and the Cangshan Mountains, and the pace is slow enough to watch clouds move across the peaks. Locals are friendly, tea-loving, and proud of Bai silverwork.
funFacts: Dali was the capital of the Nanzhao and Dali kingdoms, which ruled this part of southwest China for centuries.
Erhai Lake is one of China's largest highland lakes and is surrounded by Bai minority villages.
Dali is famous for its marble, and the Chinese word for marble literally means 'Dali stone.'

dialect.meaning: A friendly hello in Bai language, often used by locals in the old town.
Tea — the Bai three-course tea ceremony is a famous local tradition.
Delicious — locals love to hear visitors praise Bai dishes.

famousPeople.name: Duan Zhixing
famousPeople.desc: A ruler of the Dali Kingdom who promoted Buddhism and culture in the region.

famousPeople.name: Yang Shen
famousPeople.desc: A Ming dynasty scholar exiled to Yunnan wrote about Dali's landscapes and history.

famousPeople.name: Zhao Fan
famousPeople.desc: A Qing dynasty official who wrote one of the earliest detailed accounts of Dali's culture.

xishuangbanna.localVibe: Xishuangbanna is China's slice of Southeast Asia — hot, green, and full of Dai culture. Locals wear bright sarongs, drink sticky rice wine, and celebrate the Water Splashing Festival like nowhere else. The air smells of tropical flowers, durian, and grilled river fish.
funFacts: Xishuangbanna is the only region in China with tropical rainforest, hosting elephants, peacocks, and gibbons.
The Dai Water Splashing Festival marks the New Year and turns the streets into a city-wide water fight.
The name Xishuangbanna comes from the Dai language and means 'Twelve Thousand Rice Fields.'

dialect.meaning: Hello — Dai language greeting, similar to Thai.
Thank you — a Dai phrase visitors quickly learn.
Eat rice / let's eat — reflecting Dai food culture.

famousPeople.name: Zhao Shuliu
famousPeople.desc: A Dai writer and poet who documented the region's folklore and natural beauty.

famousPeople.name: Peacock Princess
famousPeople.desc: A legendary Dai folk figure celebrated in dance and story across Xishuangbanna.

famousPeople.name: Zhang Zhengxiang
famousPeople.desc: A local conservationist who helped protect the region's wild elephants and rainforests.

urumqi.localVibe: Urumqi is the farthest major city from the sea, a Central Asian frontier town that became a big city. Locals are a mix of Han, Uyghur, Kazakh, and Hui, and the food scene is heavy on lamb, naan, and pilaf. It's gritty, sunny, and proud of its Silk Road heritage.
funFacts: Urumqi is the capital of Xinjiang and one of the cities farthest from any ocean in the world.
The Xinjiang International Grand Bazaar is one of the largest bazaars in the world, blending Central Asian and Chinese commerce.
The city sits on the ancient Silk Road, and Uyghur, Kazakh, and Han cultures have mixed here for centuries.

dialect.meaning: Thank you — useful in bazaars and restaurants.

famousPeople.name: Amannisa Khan
famousPeople.desc: A legendary 16th-century Uyghur musician and poet who compiled the Twelve Muqam, a masterpiece of Uyghur classical music.

famousPeople.name: Mahmut Kashgari
famousPeople.desc: An 11th-century Turkic scholar from Xinjiang who wrote the first comprehensive dictionary of Turkic languages.

famousPeople.name: Aihemaiti
famousPeople.desc: A modern Uyghur singer from Xinjiang whose music became popular across China.

zhangjiajie.localVibe: Zhangjiajie is the city that looks like a fantasy movie. Towering sandstone pillars rise from the fog, and locals are used to sharing their hometown with Avatar fans. It's a small city with a big natural reputation, and people here are proud, hospitable, and a bit amused by the Hollywood attention.
funFacts: Zhangjiajie National Forest Park's pillar-like mountains inspired the floating Hallelujah Mountains in James Cameron's Avatar.
The park is part of a UNESCO Global Geopark and was China's first national forest park.
The glass bridge over the Grand Canyon is one of the longest and highest glass-bottomed bridges in the world.

dialect.meaning: Have you eaten? — the standard friendly greeting in Hunan style.
Girl / young woman — a friendly Hunan term.
Boy / young man — common in the region.

famousPeople.name: He Long
famousPeople.desc: A famous Hunan-born military leader and one of the ten marshals of the People's Republic of China.

famousPeople.name: Yuan Longping
famousPeople.desc: The 'Father of Hybrid Rice,' born in Jiangxi but closely associated with Hunan's agricultural research, changed global food security.

famousPeople.name: Shen Congwen
famousPeople.desc: A beloved modern writer from nearby Fenghuang who wrote about the landscapes and people of western Hunan.

shiyan.localVibe: Shiyan is a mountain city famous as the gateway to Wudang Mountain. Locals are practical, proud of their Taoist heritage, and used to living among misty peaks. Life is slower than in Wuhan, and the air carries the smell of pine and incense from the mountain temples.
funFacts: Wudang Mountain near Shiyan is the birthplace of Wudang martial arts and one of the most important Taoist sites in China.
The mountain complex is a UNESCO World Heritage site and was the setting for many kung fu films.
Shiyan is also known as China's 'Motor City' and is a major producer of trucks and auto parts.

dialect.meaning: Have you eaten? — Hubei dialect, showing local warmth.
What are you doing? — Shiyan/Hubei style.
Pretty good — common in central China.

famousPeople.name: Zhang Sanfeng
famousPeople.desc: The legendary Taoist monk credited with creating Wudang martial arts and Tai Chi is closely tied to Wudang Mountain.

famousPeople.name: Li Daoyuan
famousPeople.desc: A Northern Wei dynasty geographer who wrote about the Han River region near Shiyan.

famousPeople.name: Meng Haoran
famousPeople.desc: A famous Tang dynasty poet from nearby Xiangyang who wrote about the mountains and rivers of the region.

changzhou.localVibe: Changzhou is a tidy, prosperous Jiangsu city between Nanjing and Suzhou. Locals are proud of their dinosaur park, fine embroidery, and a balanced mix of old canals and modern industry. It's less touristy than its neighbors, which makes it feel authentically liveable.
funFacts: Changzhou is home to the China Dinosaur Park, one of Asia's largest dinosaur-themed amusement parks.
The city has a history of fine embroidery and was an important center of the Yangtze River delta economy.
Changzhou is one of the cities on the Grand Canal, which connected Beijing to Hangzhou for over a thousand years.

dialect.meaning: Hello — a Suzhou/Wuxi/Changzhou Jiangsu dialect greeting.
Very good / clever — common in Jiangsu dialect.
To play / have fun — classic Jiangsu expression.

famousPeople.name: Qu Qiubai
famousPeople.desc: A revolutionary writer and early leader of the Chinese Communist Party was born in Changzhou.

famousPeople.name: Zhao Yuanren
famousPeople.desc: A famous linguist and musician from Changzhou who made major contributions to modern Chinese phonology.

famousPeople.name: Hua Luogeng
famousPeople.desc: A world-renowned mathematician born in Jintan, near Changzhou, who overcame poverty to become a great scholar.

yangzhou.localVibe: Yangzhou is the old money of Jiangsu — refined, slow, and proud of its gardens, canals, and early morning tea culture. Locals know how to live well: walking by Slender West Lake, eating steamed dumplings, and debating the best fried rice. The city carries itself like a retired scholar.
funFacts: Yangzhou was one of the wealthiest cities in Tang and Qing dynasties, thanks to the salt trade and the Grand Canal.
Yangzhou fried rice is famous worldwide, but locals insist the real version is much more delicate than the takeaway version.
The Slender West Lake is a UNESCO-recognized cultural landscape and has inspired poets for over a thousand years.

dialect.phrase: 乖乖隆地咚 (guāi guai lóng dì dōng)
dialect.meaning: Wow / my goodness — a very Yangzhou expression of surprise.
Don't — a charming Jiangsu dialect word.

famousPeople.name: Zheng Banqiao
famousPeople.desc: One of the Eight Eccentrics of Yangzhou, a famous Qing dynasty painter and calligrapher.

famousPeople.name: Jiang Chunlin
famousPeople.desc: A salt merchant and philanthropist who helped build many of Yangzhou's gardens.

famousPeople.name: Li Bingheng
famousPeople.desc: A Qing dynasty official from Yangzhou known for his role in modernizing China's navy.

ningbo.localVibe: Ningbo is a wealthy port city with a deep merchant history. Locals are practical, well-traveled, and proud of their seafood and rice dumplings. The city is quieter than Shanghai but has its own maritime swagger, with old foreign concessions and a bustling modern port.
funFacts: Ningbo is one of China's oldest ports and was a major departure point for Chinese emigrants to Japan and Southeast Asia.
Tianyi Ge in Ningbo is one of the oldest surviving private libraries in Asia, founded in 1561.
Ningbo rice dumplings and stinky tofu are famous throughout China.

dialect.meaning: Hello — similar to Shanghainese, as Ningbo dialect belongs to the same Wu family.
Gimmick / flashy — a common Wu-dialect word.

famousPeople.name: Pan Tianshou
famousPeople.desc: One of modern China's greatest painters and art educators was born in Ningbo.

famousPeople.name: Tong Dizhou
famousPeople.desc: A pioneering Chinese biologist and cloning researcher from Ningbo.

famousPeople.name: Shao Yifu
famousPeople.desc: The Hong Kong entertainment and philanthropy tycoon was born in Ningbo and donated to schools across China.

wuxi.localVibe: Wuxi is a wealthy, lake-loving city on the shores of Taihu. Locals are proud of their sweet spare ribs, their Buddhist giant statue, and the fact that they live well without boasting. It's the Jiangsu city that prefers good food over flashy skyline.
funFacts: Wuxi is famous for the Grand Buddha at Ling Shan, one of China's largest bronze Buddha statues.
The city sits on Lake Tai, China's third-largest freshwater lake, and has long been a center of silk and grain trade.
Wuxi-style spare ribs are sweet, red, and so beloved that locals claim no visitor should leave without trying them.

famousPeople.name: Gu Kaizhi
famousPeople.desc: A famous Eastern Jin dynasty painter from Wuxi, considered one of the founders of Chinese figure painting.

famousPeople.name: Xu Beihong
famousPeople.desc: One of China's most celebrated modern painters, born in Yixing near Wuxi, known for his powerful horse paintings.

famousPeople.name: Qian Zhongshu
famousPeople.desc: A brilliant 20th-century writer and scholar from Wuxi, best known for the novel Fortress Besieged.

xuzhou.localVibe: Xuzhou is a northern city with a deep Han dynasty soul. Locals are proud, beer-loving, and surrounded by ancient tomb art. The city feels like a crossroads between the refined south and the hearty north.
funFacts: Xuzhou was the hometown of Liu Bang, the founder of the Han dynasty, and many Han dynasty tombs have been found here.
The Terracotta Warriors of Xi'an are more famous, but Xuzhou has its own impressive Han dynasty terracotta army.
Xuzhou is one of the cities on the Grand Canal and was historically a key military and transport hub.

dialect.meaning: What are you doing? — northern style.

famousPeople.name: Liu Bang (Emperor Gaozu of Han)
famousPeople.desc: The founder of the Han dynasty, one of China's greatest emperors, was born near Xuzhou.

famousPeople.name: Xiang Yu
famousPeople.desc: The legendary warrior king who battled Liu Bang for control of China was also from the Xuzhou region.

famousPeople.name: Li Keqiang
famousPeople.desc: The former premier of China was born in Dingyuan, Anhui, but his career connected him to the broader central China region.

wenzhou.localVibe: Wenzhou is China's legendary business city. Locals are famous for being sharp traders, noodle soup lovers, and speakers of a dialect so difficult that even other Chinese people struggle to understand it. The city is wealthy, entrepreneurial, and full of coastal energy.
funFacts: Wenzhou merchants are famous across China for starting small businesses and building global trade networks.
The city is known for its light manufacturing, especially shoes, eyeglasses, and lighters.
Wenzhou's Yandang Mountain is one of China's most famous scenic mountains and a UNESCO Global Geopark.

dialect.meaning: Hello — Wu dialect, though Wenzhou dialect is famously hard even for Wu speakers.

famousPeople.name: Nan Huai-Chin
famousPeople.desc: A famous Buddhist scholar and spiritual teacher born in Yueqing, near Wenzhou.

famousPeople.name: Liu Yong
famousPeople.desc: A Song dynasty poet and official known for his romantic ci poetry, associated with the Wenzhou region.

famousPeople.name: Wang Jianlin
famousPeople.desc: The billionaire founder of Wanda Group was born in Sichuan, but Wenzhou's business culture mirrors his entrepreneurial drive.

yantai.localVibe: Yantai is a port city on the Bohai Strait where seafood, wine, and colonial architecture come together. Locals are relaxed, proud of their apples and grapes, and live with one eye on the sea. It feels like a mini-Qingdao with fewer crowds.
funFacts: Yantai is one of China's largest wine-producing regions, and the Changyu Wine Company, founded in 1892, is the country's oldest winery.
Penglai Pavilion, a famous ancient complex near Yantai, is tied to legends of the Eight Immortals crossing the sea.
Yantai apples are famous across China for their crisp sweetness.

dialect.meaning: Hello — standard Mandarin, but with a Shandong lilt.
Good / okay — common in northern Shandong.

famousPeople.name: Zhang Yuzhe
famousPeople.desc: A famous astronomer from Yantai known as the father of modern Chinese astronomy.

famousPeople.name: Zhang Jian
famousPeople.desc: A Qing dynasty entrepreneur and modernizer from nearby Nantong had strong ties to Shandong's coastal economy.

famousPeople.name: Changyu Winery
famousPeople.desc: Founded by Zhang Bishi in 1892, it made Yantai the birthplace of Chinese wine.

weihai.localVibe: Weihai is a clean, coastal city at the tip of the Shandong Peninsula. Locals are proud of their fresh air, seafood, and history as a former British naval base. The city feels calm, orderly, and a bit like a beach town that takes its history seriously.
funFacts: Weihai was leased to Britain from 1898 to 1930 as a naval base, and British-style buildings still remain.
The city is famous for being one of China's cleanest and most livable coastal cities.
Liugong Island, just offshore, is a major site of China's First Sino-Japanese War history.

dialect.meaning: Have you eaten? — standard northern greeting.

famousPeople.name: Deng Shichang
famousPeople.desc: A Qing dynasty naval officer who died heroically in the First Sino-Japanese War is commemorated on Liugong Island.

famousPeople.name: Zhang Zhidong
famousPeople.desc: A late Qing reformer and governor who strengthened China's coastal defenses, including in the Weihai area.

famousPeople.name: Guo Moruo
famousPeople.desc: A famous modern Chinese writer and scholar visited Weihai and wrote about its history.

shijiazhuang.localVibe: Shijiazhuang is a young provincial capital built by railways. Locals are practical, proud of their growing role as a transport hub, and surrounded by the history of Hebei province. It's a working city with quick access to ancient wonders.
funFacts: Shijiazhuang became the capital of Hebei only in 1968, making it one of China's youngest provincial capitals.
The city is a major railway hub connecting Beijing, Taiyuan, Jinan, and Zhengzhou.
The famous Zhaozhou Bridge, the world's oldest surviving open-spandrel stone arch bridge, is near Shijiazhuang.

dialect.meaning: What are you doing? — northern style.

famousPeople.name: Zhao Yun
famousPeople.desc: A legendary general of the Three Kingdoms period, said to be from Zhengding, near Shijiazhuang.

famousPeople.name: Zhou Enlai
famousPeople.desc: The beloved premier had deep ties to the revolutionary history of the Hebei region.

famousPeople.name: Bai Juyi
famousPeople.desc: The Tang dynasty poet was connected to the broader Hebei region through his official postings.

tangshan.localVibe: Tangshan is a tough, industrial city that rebuilt itself after the devastating 1976 earthquake. Locals are resilient, proud of their steel and porcelain, and surprisingly fond of their own dialect and seafood. It's a city of second chances.
funFacts: Tangshan was hit by one of the deadliest earthquakes in modern history in 1976, killing hundreds of thousands and nearly leveling the city.
The city is one of China's largest producers of steel and ceramics.
Tangshan is close to the Eastern Qing Tombs, the burial site of several Qing dynasty emperors.

dialect.meaning: What are you doing? — Northeastern/Hebei blend.

famousPeople.name: Li Dazhao
famousPeople.desc: A founder of the Chinese Communist Party was born in Leting, near Tangshan.

famousPeople.name: Wang Guowei
famousPeople.desc: A famous modern Chinese scholar and poet, though more associated with Zhejiang, had intellectual ties to the northern literary world.

famousPeople.name: Tangshan Earthquake Survivors
famousPeople.desc: The resilience of ordinary Tangshan people became a symbol of Chinese national strength after 1976.

qinhuangdao.localVibe: Qinhuangdao is where the Great Wall meets the sea. Locals are proud of their beach town status, their fresh seafood, and their role as a summer retreat for Beijingers. It's a city that balances history, ports, and sand.
funFacts: Qinhuangdao is named after Qin Shi Huang, the first emperor of China, who sent expeditions to find immortality from this coast.
Laolongtou, the eastern starting point of the Ming Great Wall, extends into the sea here.
Qinhuangdao's Beidaihe district has long been a summer retreat for Chinese leaders.

famousPeople.name: Qin Shi Huang
famousPeople.desc: The first emperor of China sent alchemists from this coast to search for the elixir of immortality.

famousPeople.name: Mao Zedong
famousPeople.desc: The Chinese leader spent many summers in Beidaihe and wrote poems inspired by the sea.

famousPeople.name: Zhang Xueliang
famousPeople.desc: The Young Marshal was briefly held under house arrest in the Qinhuangdao area.

hohhot.localVibe: Hohhot is where the grasslands meet the city. Locals are proud of their Mongol heritage, love milk tea and lamb, and balance Mongolian culture with modern Chinese life. The air smells of dairy and roasted meat.
funFacts: Hohhot means 'Blue City' in Mongolian and is the capital of Inner Mongolia.
The city is famous for its dairy industry, including brands like Yili and Mengniu that are now global names.
The Dazhao Temple, built in the 16th century, is one of the most important Tibetan Buddhist temples in Inner Mongolia.

dialect.meaning: How are you? — polite Mongolian phrase.

famousPeople.name: Genghis Khan
famousPeople.desc: The Mongol Empire founder's legacy is honored throughout Inner Mongolia, and Hohhot hosts many Mongol cultural institutions.

famousPeople.name: Borjigin Shuluun
famousPeople.desc: A modern Inner Mongolian writer and historian who documented Mongolian culture.

famousPeople.name: Ulan Muqir
famousPeople.desc: The Red Budia performing troupe, a famous Inner Mongolian cultural group, has performed in Hohhot for decades.

foshan.localVibe: Foshan is the kung fu and ceramic heart of the Pearl River Delta. Locals are proud, practical, and obsessed with food — especially their own brand of Cantonese cuisine. The city feels like Guangzhou's more traditional cousin.
funFacts: Foshan is the birthplace of wing chun kung fu, associated with the legendary Ip Man and Bruce Lee's teacher.
The city is one of the world's largest producers of ceramics and bathroom fixtures.
Foshan is famous for its martial arts schools, lion dance teams, and ancient Zumiao Temple.

dialect.phrase: 食咗饭未 (sik6 zo2 faan6 mei6)

famousPeople.name: Ip Man
famousPeople.desc: The legendary wing chun master who taught Bruce Lee was born in Foshan.

famousPeople.name: Bruce Lee
famousPeople.desc: Though born in San Francisco, Lee's martial arts roots trace back to his father's Foshan heritage and Ip Man's school.

famousPeople.name: Huang Feihong
famousPeople.desc: The folk hero and martial artist of Cantonese legend is strongly associated with Foshan.

dongguan.localVibe: Dongguan is the factory floor of the Pearl River Delta — fast, young, and full of people from across China. Locals work hard, eat late, and unwind at noisy barbecue stalls. It's not pretty, but it's where a lot of modern China was made.
funFacts: Dongguan was once known as the 'world's factory' for electronics, toys, shoes, and furniture.
Humen, part of Dongguan, was where Lin Zexu destroyed British opium before the First Opium War.
The city has transformed from a manufacturing hub into a tech and innovation center.

dialect.phrase: 食咗饭未 (sik6 zo2 faan6 mei6)

famousPeople.name: Lin Zexu
famousPeople.desc: The Qing dynasty anti-opium official destroyed foreign opium at Humen in Dongguan.

famousPeople.name: Yuan Chonghuan
famousPeople.desc: A Ming dynasty general born in Dongguan who defended the dynasty against Manchu invasion.

famousPeople.name: Dongguan Entrepreneurs
famousPeople.desc: Countless factory owners and tech founders built their fortunes in Dongguan's manufacturing boom.

huizhou.localVibe: Huizhou is a lakeside city between Shenzhen and the mountains. Locals are relaxed, proud of their West Lake (a smaller namesake of Hangzhou's), and enjoy Dongjiang salt-baked chicken. It feels like a weekend escape city that grew up.
funFacts: Huizhou's West Lake has been praised by poets since the Song dynasty, including Su Dongpo.
The city is one of the fastest-growing in Guangdong and a popular destination for Shenzhen weekenders.
Huizhou is known for electronics, petrochemicals, and beautiful coastal areas like Xunliao Bay.

dialect.phrase: 食咗饭未 (sik6 zo2 faan6 mei6)

famousPeople.name: Su Shi (Su Dongpo)
famousPeople.desc: The Song dynasty poet was exiled to Huizhou and wrote about its lake and scenery.

famousPeople.name: Ye Ting
famousPeople.desc: A famous revolutionary general from Huizhou who played a key role in the Northern Expedition.

famousPeople.name: Teng Daiyuan
famousPeople.desc: A modern military leader and politician from Huizhou.

guiyang.localVibe: Guiyang is a mountain city that has grown fast while staying affordable. Locals love spicy sour fish soup, late-night barbecues, and complaining about the constant drizzle. The city is surrounded by karst hills and feels like a gateway to Guizhou's wild nature.
funFacts: Guiyang is the capital of Guizhou, one of China's most mountainous and ethnically diverse provinces.
The city is known as China's 'Big Data Valley' because many tech companies have data centers in its cool climate.
Huangguoshu Waterfall, one of China's largest, is a few hours from Guiyang.

dialect.meaning: What are you doing? — Guizhou style.
Great / excellent — also common in Yunnan.

famousPeople.name: Wang Yangming
famousPeople.desc: The famous Ming dynasty philosopher and general was exiled to Guizhou and developed his ideas there.

famousPeople.name: Zhang Xueliang
famousPeople.desc: The Young Marshal was held under house arrest in the mountains of Guizhou.

famousPeople.name: Ding Baozhen
famousPeople.desc: The Qing official after whom the famous kung pao chicken is named was from Guizhou.

zunyi.localVibe: Zunyi is a proud, spicy city in northern Guizhou. Locals love maotai liquor, lamb rice noodles, and talking about the famous 1935 Zunyi Conference. It's a city of revolutionary history tucked into steep green hills.
funFacts: Zunyi is famous for Moutai (Maotai) liquor, China's national spirit, produced in the nearby town of Maotai.
The 1935 Zunyi Conference during the Long March reshaped the leadership of the Chinese Communist Party.
Zunyi mutton rice noodles are a beloved breakfast across the city.

dialect.meaning: What are you doing? — Guizhou style.

famousPeople.name: Mao Zedong
famousPeople.desc: Mao regained influence at the 1935 Zunyi Conference, a turning point in the Long March.

famousPeople.name: Zhou Enlai
famousPeople.desc: Zhou played a key role at the Zunyi Conference.

famousPeople.name: Zunyi Liquor Makers
famousPeople.desc: Generations of distillers in Maotai, near Zunyi, created China's most famous baijiu.

huzhou.localVibe: Huzhou is a quiet Jiangsu-Zhejiang border city famous for silk, tea, and Taihu Lake. Locals are gentle, proud of their freshwater fish, and live at a slower pace than neighbors Hangzhou or Suzhou. The city is a good place to see the softer side of the Yangtze delta.
funFacts: Huzhou has been a center of silk production for over 4,700 years.
The city is famous for Taihu Lake's 'three whites' — whitefish, white shrimp, and whitebait.
Huzhou's Mogan Mountain is a popular retreat for Shanghai and Hangzhou residents.

famousPeople.name: Su Shi (Su Dongpo)
famousPeople.desc: The Song poet served as an official in Huzhou and wrote famous poems there.

famousPeople.name: Zhao Mengfu
famousPeople.desc: A Yuan dynasty painter and calligrapher from Huzhou, one of China's greatest artists.

famousPeople.name: Chen Qiyou
famousPeople.desc: A modern Huzhou-born writer and educator.

jiaxing.localVibe: Jiaxing is a water town between Shanghai and Hangzhou, famous for red rice, sticky rice cakes, and a slow canal life. Locals are proud of their South Lake, where the Chinese Communist Party held its first National Congress on a boat. The city feels like a historical postcard with modern industry.
funFacts: Jiaxing's South Lake is known as the birthplace of the Chinese Communist Party, where the first party congress concluded on a boat in 1921.
The city is famous for zongzi (sticky rice dumplings), especially during the Dragon Boat Festival.
Jiaxing is home to Wuzhen, one of China's most famous ancient water towns.

famousPeople.name: Mao Zedong
famousPeople.desc: The young Mao attended the final sessions of the first CCP congress in Jiaxing's South Lake.

famousPeople.name: Wang Guowei
famousPeople.desc: A famous modern Chinese scholar and poet, though more associated with Haining near Jiaxing.

famousPeople.name: Mao Dun
famousPeople.desc: The renowned 20th-century writer was born in Wuzhen, Jiaxing.

jinhua.localVibe: Jinhua is a busy Zhejiang city surrounded by hills and famous for ham. Locals are practical, proud of their dried ham, and linked to the ancient trade routes that passed through the region. It's less polished than Hangzhou but full of honest flavor.
funFacts: Jinhua ham is one of China's most famous cured meats, prized for its rich red color and flavor.
The city is an important logistics and trade hub in inland Zhejiang.
Jinhua's nearby village of诸葛八卦村 (Zhuge Bagua Village) is a historic maze-like village.

famousPeople.name: Zhu Geliang (Zhuge Liang)
famousPeople.desc: The legendary Three Kingdoms strategist's descendants settled in Zhuge Village near Jinhua.

famousPeople.name: Luo Binwang
famousPeople.desc: One of the Four Great Poets of the Early Tang dynasty was born in Jinhua.

famousPeople.name: Ai Qing
famousPeople.desc: The famous modern Chinese poet was born in Jinhua's Jinhua village.

jining.localVibe: Jining is the hometown of Confucius and Mencius, and it feels like it. Locals are proud of their history, respectful of tradition, and love their wheat pancakes and canal-side life. The city sits on the Grand Canal and carries the weight of 2,500 years of Chinese culture.
funFacts: Jining is the birthplace of Confucius, the most influential philosopher in Chinese history, in nearby Qufu.
The city is also associated with Mencius, another major Confucian thinker, from nearby Zoucheng.
Jining was an important hub on the Grand Canal, connecting northern and southern China.

famousPeople.name: Confucius
famousPeople.desc: The founder of Confucianism was born in Qufu, near Jining, and shaped Chinese culture for millennia.

famousPeople.name: Mencius
famousPeople.desc: The second great Confucian philosopher was born in Zoucheng, also near Jining.

famousPeople.name: Zhang Xueliang
famousPeople.desc: The Young Marshal had connections to Shandong's military history.

shenyang.localVibe: Shenyang is the proud old capital of Manchuria. Locals are hearty, funny, and proud of their imperial palace and heavy industry. Winters are brutal, but the city is warm in personality — big on barbecue, beer, and straight talk.
funFacts: Shenyang's Imperial Palace is a UNESCO site and the former palace of the early Qing dynasty before they moved to Beijing.
The city is famous for its 9.18 Historical Museum, marking the 1931 Japanese invasion of Manchuria.
Shenyang was one of China's first heavy industrial centers and is still known for aerospace and machine manufacturing.

dialect.meaning: What are you doing? — Northeastern directness.

famousPeople.name: Nurhaci
famousPeople.desc: The founder of the Later Jin dynasty, which became the Qing dynasty, built his capital in Shenyang.

famousPeople.name: Huang Taiji
famousPeople.desc: Nurhaci's son moved the Qing capital from Shenyang to Beijing.

famousPeople.name: Zhao Benshan
famousPeople.desc: China's most famous comedian and xiaopin performer was born in Liaoning, near Shenyang.

changchun.localVibe: Changchun is the 'Automobile City' of China, built on wide Soviet-style streets and Manchukuo history. Locals are practical, proud of their film studio, and enjoy a cold but livable northern city. It's where China's first cars rolled off the line.
funFacts: Changchun was the capital of the Japanese puppet state of Manchukuo from 1932 to 1945, and the imperial palace remains.
FAW (First Automobile Works), China's oldest car manufacturer, was founded in Changchun in 1953.
Changchun Film Studio was one of the cradle of Chinese cinema, producing many classic films.

famousPeople.name: Puyi
famousPeople.desc: The last emperor of China lived as the puppet emperor of Manchukuo in Changchun.

famousPeople.name: Liu Changchun
famousPeople.desc: China's first Olympic athlete, sent to the 1932 Los Angeles Olympics, had ties to the region.

famousPeople.name: Changchun Film Studio Directors
famousPeople.desc: Generations of Chinese filmmakers shaped national cinema from Changchun.

luoyang.localVibe: Luoyang is one of China's ancient capitals, where peonies, Tang dynasty glamour, and Buddhist cave art meet modern industrial life. Locals are proud of their long history, love spicy soup, and treat the annual Peony Festival like a city-wide holiday.
funFacts: Luoyang was the capital of 13 Chinese dynasties and is one of the Four Great Ancient Capitals of China.
The Longmen Grottoes, a UNESCO site, contain over 100,000 Buddhist statues carved into cliffs.
Luoyang is known as the 'City of Peonies' and hosts a famous peony festival every spring.

famousPeople.name: Laozi
famousPeople.desc: The legendary founder of Taoism is traditionally said to have lived in the Luoyang area.

famousPeople.name: Du Fu
famousPeople.desc: One of China's greatest poets spent formative years in the Luoyang region during the Tang dynasty.

famousPeople.name: Li Bai
famousPeople.desc: The famous Tang poet also had connections to the Luoyang court and literary circles.

kaifeng.localVibe: Kaifeng is a Song dynasty time capsule. Locals are proud of their ancient city walls, night markets, and the fact that their city was once the largest in the world. The feeling is historic, slightly sleepy, and full of dumpling shops.
funFacts: Kaifeng was the capital of the Northern Song dynasty and may have been the world's largest city around the year 1000.
The city is famous for its night market and traditional snacks like soup dumplings and almond tea.
Kaifeng has one of China's oldest Jewish communities, with a small synagogue site still remembered.

famousPeople.name: Bao Zheng (Lord Bao)
famousPeople.desc: The legendary honest judge served as an official in Kaifeng, and his court is a major tourist attraction.

famousPeople.name: Zhang Zeduan
famousPeople.desc: The painter of 'Along the River During the Qingming Festival' captured the bustle of Kaifeng-era life.

famousPeople.name: Li Shizhen
famousPeople.desc: The famous Ming dynasty pharmacologist had connections to the broader Henan region.

nanyang.localVibe: Nanyang is a big, unpretentious Henan city surrounded by farmland and history. Locals are proud of their jade carving, medical sage heritage, and being a crossroads between north and south. Life is straightforward, hearty, and centered on good noodles.
funFacts: Nanyang is famous for its Dushan jade, one of the four famous jades of China.
The city is associated with Zhang Zhongjing, the 'Sage of Medicine' of the Han dynasty, who wrote a foundational Chinese medical text.
Nanyang is one of the birthplaces of the Chu culture and has deep roots in Han dynasty history.

famousPeople.name: Zhang Zhongjing
famousPeople.desc: The 'Sage of Chinese Medicine' was from Nanyang and wrote the Treatise on Cold Damage Diseases.

famousPeople.name: Zhang Heng
famousPeople.desc: The Han dynasty inventor of the seismoscope and astronomer was born in Nanyang.

famousPeople.name: Zhou Enlai
famousPeople.desc: The beloved premier was born in nearby Huai'an, but his revolutionary career touched the Henan region.

taiyuan.localVibe: Taiyuan is a northern industrial city with a surprising amount of history. Locals are proud of their Shanxi merchants, vinegar, and noodles. It's a city of coal and Buddhism, where temple fairs and heavy industry coexist.
funFacts: Taiyuan was an important military and political center for over 2,500 years.
Shanxi aged vinegar, produced near Taiyuan, is one of China's four famous vinegars and is prized for its rich flavor.
The city is a gateway to the ancient Buddhist temples and cliff sculptures of Shanxi province.

famousPeople.name: Li Shimin
famousPeople.desc: The Tang emperor Taizong, one of China's greatest rulers, was connected to the Taiyuan uprising that founded the Tang dynasty.

famousPeople.name: Wang Weifang
famousPeople.desc: A modern Taiyuan-born artist and cultural figure.

famousPeople.name: Shanxi Merchants
famousPeople.desc: The powerful merchant families of Shanxi helped finance trade across northern China for centuries.

datong.localVibe: Datong is a gritty northern city with some of China's most jaw-dropping ancient art. Locals are proud of the Yungang Grottoes, their hanging temple, and their coal history. It's a city where Buddhism meets industry and dust.
funFacts: The Yungang Grottoes near Datong are a UNESCO World Heritage site with 252 caves and over 51,000 Buddhist statues.
The Hanging Temple, built into a cliff, is one of China's most remarkable architectural feats.
Datong was a frontier city for centuries and served as the capital of several northern dynasties.

famousPeople.name: Bodhidharma
famousPeople.desc: The legendary Buddhist monk credited with bringing Chan (Zen) Buddhism to China was said to have passed through the region.

famousPeople.name: Geng Yanbo
famousPeople.desc: The modern mayor who led the controversial but transformative restoration of Datong's old city walls.

famousPeople.name: Li Yuan
famousPeople.desc: The founder of the Tang dynasty launched his uprising from Taiyuan, near Datong.

chengde.localVibe: Chengde is a mountain retreat city where Qing emperors escaped the Beijing heat. Locals are proud of their imperial mountain resort, their cool summers, and a slower pace than the capital. The city feels like a historical park with a modern town attached.
funFacts: The Chengde Mountain Resort, a UNESCO site, was the summer retreat of Qing emperors and is China's largest imperial garden.
The Eight Outer Temples around the resort blend Tibetan, Han, and Mongolian architecture.
Chengde is known for its cool mountain climate and has long been a summer escape for northern China.

famousPeople.name: Kangxi Emperor
famousPeople.desc: The Qing emperor who began building the Chengde Mountain Resort as a summer retreat.

famousPeople.name: Qianlong Emperor
famousPeople.desc: Expanded the Chengde resort and used it to host Mongolian and Tibetan nobles.

famousPeople.name: Modern Chengde Conservationists
famousPeople.desc: Local historians and architects have worked to preserve Chengde's imperial heritage.

yichang.localVibe: Yichang is the gateway to the Three Gorges, a river city where freight boats, hydroelectric power, and spicy Hubei food meet. Locals are proud of their position on the Yangtze, their oranges, and the engineering marvel of the nearby dam.
funFacts: Yichang is the starting point for Yangtze River cruises through the Three Gorges.
The Three Gorges Dam, the world's largest hydroelectric dam, is near Yichang.
Yichang is famous for its citrus fruits, especially its sweet oranges and pomelos.

dialect.meaning: What are you doing? — Hubei style.

famousPeople.name: Qu Yuan
famousPeople.desc: The ancient poet of the Chu kingdom is commemorated near Yichang, and his legend is tied to the Dragon Boat Festival.

famousPeople.name: Wang Zhaojun
famousPeople.desc: One of the Four Beauties of ancient China is associated with the Xiangxi region near Yichang.

famousPeople.name: Modern Dam Engineers
famousPeople.desc: Generations of engineers built and managed the Three Gorges Dam near Yichang.

xiangyang.localVibe: Xiangyang is a city of ancient walls and Three Kingdoms romance. Locals are proud of their beef noodles, their historic fortress, and the legends of Zhuge Liang. The city feels like a place where history is still being told over bowls of soup.
funFacts: Xiangyang's ancient city walls are some of the best-preserved in China and were featured in many Three Kingdoms battles.
Zhuge Liang, the legendary strategist, is closely associated with Xiangyang and nearby Longzhong.
The city is famous for Xiangyang beef noodles, a hearty breakfast dish beloved across Hubei.

famousPeople.name: Zhuge Liang
famousPeople.desc: The legendary Three Kingdoms strategist lived and planned campaigns in Xiangyang.

famousPeople.name: Liu Bei
famousPeople.desc: The Shu Han emperor sought Zhuge Liang's counsel in the Xiangyang region.

famousPeople.name: Mi Fu
famousPeople.desc: A famous Song dynasty calligrapher and painter was from Xiangyang.

lanzhou.localVibe: Lanzhou is the gritty heart of the Silk Road, where the Yellow River cuts through a narrow valley. Locals are proud of their beef noodles, their river, and their role as a gateway between Tibet, Xinjiang, and central China. The city is busy, dusty, and full of noodle shops open at all hours.
funFacts: Lanzhou beef noodles are one of China's most famous noodle soups, and the city has entire streets of noodle shops.
The city is the only provincial capital through which the Yellow River flows.
Lanzhou was a key stop on the Silk Road and remains a hub for trains heading west to Xinjiang and Tibet.

dialect.meaning: Excellent / vigorous — a classic Lanzhou compliment.

famousPeople.name: Zhang Qian
famousPeople.desc: The Han dynasty explorer opened the Silk Road through the Gansu corridor that runs through Lanzhou.

famousPeople.name: Zhang Yimou
famousPeople.desc: The famous director was born in Xi'an but studied and began his career in the northwest, including Lanzhou.

famousPeople.name: Huang Jiguang
famousPeople.desc: A Korean War hero born in Sichuan, but Lanzhou is home to a famous memorial honoring him.

xining.localVibe: Xining is the cool, high-altitude gateway to Tibet. Locals are a mix of Han, Hui, and Tibetan, and the city feels like a meeting point between cultures. The air is thin, the mutton is good, and the mountains are always in sight.
funFacts: Xining is the capital of Qinghai province and sits at about 2,275 meters above sea level.
The city is an important railway hub on the way to Lhasa by train.
Kumbum Monastery (Ta'er Si), near Xining, is one of the most important Tibetan Buddhist monasteries outside Tibet.

dialect.meaning: Good luck / auspiciousness — Tibetan greeting used in Xining.
Excellent — also used in Gansu and Qinghai.

famousPeople.name: Tsongkhapa
famousPeople.desc: The founder of the Gelug school of Tibetan Buddhism was born near Xining, and Kumbum Monastery marks his birthplace.

famousPeople.name: Zhang Qian
famousPeople.desc: Han dynasty explorer passed through the region on the Silk Road.

famousPeople.name: Ma Bufang
famousPeople.desc: A powerful Muslim warlord who ruled Qinghai from Xining in the Republican era.

yinchuan.localVibe: Yinchuan is a calm, dusty city on the edge of the desert where Hui Muslim culture meets the Yellow River. Locals are proud of their goji berries, hand-pulled lamb noodles, and the mysterious Western Xia dynasty that once ruled here. The city feels like a history book that has been partly sandblasted.
funFacts: Yinchuan was the capital of the Western Xia dynasty, a mysterious kingdom that ruled from 1038 to 1227.
The Western Xia Tombs, known as the 'Pyramids of China,' are a major archaeological site nearby.
Ningxia is one of China's main goji berry production regions.

famousPeople.name: Emperor Yuanhao of Western Xia
famousPeople.desc: The founder of the Western Xia dynasty made Yinchuan his capital.

famousPeople.name: Hui Merchants
famousPeople.desc: Generations of Hui traders built the overland trade networks linking Yinchuan to Central Asia.

famousPeople.name: Ma Benzhai
famousPeople.desc: A Hui Muslim resistance commander against Japanese invasion during World War II.

kashgar.localVibe: Kashgar is the westernmost city of China and feels like Central Asia more than the east. Locals are Uyghur, Hui, and Han, and the Sunday bazaar, mosque, and old city alleys are full of music, bread, and dried fruit. The city is dusty, ancient, and proud of its Silk Road soul.
funFacts: Kashgar is closer to Baghdad than to Beijing and has been a Silk Road hub for over 2,000 years.
The Id Kah Mosque in Kashgar is one of the largest mosques in China.
Kashgar's Sunday livestock market is one of the liveliest traditional markets in Central Asia.

famousPeople.name: Mahmud Kashgari
famousPeople.desc: The 11th-century Turkic scholar wrote the first comprehensive dictionary of Turkic languages and was from Kashgar.

famousPeople.name: Amannisa Khan
famousPeople.desc: The legendary Uyghur musician and poet compiled the Twelve Muqam.

famousPeople.name: Marco Polo
famousPeople.desc: The Venetian traveler passed through Kashgar and described its markets and people.

quanzhou.localVibe: Quanzhou is a port city with more layers of history than most Chinese cities. Locals are proud of their maritime Silk Road past, their temples, and their noodle shops. The city is relaxed, religiously diverse, and full of old stone streets and colonial-era houses.
funFacts: Quanzhou was one of the world's largest ports during the Song and Yuan dynasties and a key node on the maritime Silk Road.
The city is home to temples of Buddhism, Taoism, Islam, Manichaeism, and Christianity, all within a small area.
Quanzhou is famous for its Zayton, a name used by Marco Polo and medieval travelers.

famousPeople.name: Li Zhi
famousPeople.desc: A Ming dynasty philosopher and rebel thinker from Quanzhou who challenged Confucian orthodoxy.

famousPeople.name: Koxinga (Zheng Chenggong)
famousPeople.desc: The Ming loyalist who expelled the Dutch from Taiwan was born in nearby Nan'an, Quanzhou.

famousPeople.name: Marco Polo
famousPeople.desc: The Venetian traveler described Quanzhou as one of the greatest ports of the world.

nantong.localVibe: Nantong is a Jiangsu river city with a strong merchant and education tradition. Locals are proud of their textiles, their Hao River scenery, and being one of the first modern Chinese cities opened to industry. It feels like a smaller, calmer version of Suzhou with a business edge.
funFacts: Nantong was one of the first cities in China to modernize its industry, thanks to the reformer Zhang Jian in the late 19th century.
The city is famous for its blue calico cloth, a traditional textile craft still practiced today.
Nantong's Hao River is one of the most complete ancient city moats in China.

famousPeople.name: Zhang Jian
famousPeople.desc: A Qing dynasty scholar, industrialist, and reformer who turned Nantong into a model modern city.

famousPeople.name: Zhang Xu
famousPeople.desc: A Tang dynasty calligrapher known as the 'Sage of Cursive Script' was from the Nantong area.

famousPeople.name: Luo Yi
famousPeople.desc: A modern Nantong-born entrepreneur and educator continuing the city's commercial tradition.

shaoxing.localVibe: Shaoxing is a city of canals, rice wine, and literature. Locals are proud of their yellow wine, their old bridges, and the fact that Lu Xun and many other writers came from here. The city feels like a quieter, more bookish version of Suzhou.
funFacts: Shaoxing is famous for its huangjiu (yellow rice wine), one of China's most traditional alcoholic drinks.
Lu Xun, China's greatest modern writer, was born in Shaoxing, and his former home is now a museum.
The city is known for its stone bridges, black-tiled boats, and canal-side architecture.

famousPeople.name: Lu Xun
famousPeople.desc: China's greatest modern writer was born in Shaoxing and wrote many of his famous works about the city.

famousPeople.name: Wang Xizhi
famousPeople.desc: The 'Sage of Calligraphy' from the Jin dynasty is associated with Shaoxing and the Orchid Pavilion.

famousPeople.name: Qiu Jin
famousPeople.desc: The revolutionary feminist and poet was born in Shaoxing and became a martyr of the anti-Qing movement.

leshan.localVibe: Leshan is a Sichuan city dominated by the world's largest stone Buddha carved into a cliff. Locals are proud of their spicy food, their river, and the giant statue that watches over the confluence of three rivers. It's a tourist city that still feels lived-in.
funFacts: The Leshan Giant Buddha is the largest stone Buddha in the world, carved over 90 years during the Tang dynasty.
The Buddha was built to calm the dangerous waters where the Min, Dadu, and Qingyi rivers meet.
Leshan is also famous for its spicy tofu, grilled fish, and Sichuan hot pot.

dialect.phrase: 摆龙门阵 (bǎi lóng mén zhèn)

famousPeople.name: Haitong Monk
famousPeople.desc: The Tang dynasty monk who began the construction of the Leshan Giant Buddha to protect sailors.

famousPeople.name: Li Bing
famousPeople.desc: The Qin dynasty engineer who built the Dujiangyan irrigation system also shaped water management in the region.

famousPeople.name: Su Shi
famousPeople.desc: The Song poet visited Leshan and wrote about its Buddha and rivers.

mianyang.localVibe: Mianyang is a Sichuan city of science, technology, and surprising natural beauty. Locals are proud of their aerospace industry, their nearby mountains, and their relaxed Sichuan lifestyle. It's a smart city that knows how to take a long lunch.
